purpose: Record recent Abra River FishCoRe leads while separating aggregate goby catch share, source-reported bunog identification and management discussion from validated occurrences, stock assessment, current rules and public data.

geographicScope.note: The February BFAR notice describes the Abra River System as spanning CAR and Region I; no mapped management/study boundary is supplied.

catchEvidence.interpretation: BFAR-reported group aggregate only; not a species-specific share, reach occurrence, catch per unit effort, current abundance or stock condition.

policyLead.scopeAsReported: Goby fry (ipon) fishery of the Abra River System in Regions I and CAR
draftBriefsAsReported: Small Fish, Big Impact: Why the Abra River’s Goby Fishery Needs Action Now
Regulating Fine Mesh Net – Not Totally Banning for the Goby Fry Harvesting in the Ilocos Region

bunogManagement.recommendationAsReported: The notice reports a management recommendation to eliminate electrofishing activities in the Abra River.

evidenceLimits: March's 20.22 percent is for gobies as a group; do not assign it to Awaous melanocephalus or bunog.
The notices do not provide species-by-site, station, landing-center or reach records.
The 4 percent biomass and 28 percent limit reference point cannot be independently interpreted without metric definition, method, sampled reach, time series and uncertainty.
The 13.5 cm maturity value and gear-use figures lack supporting data/methods in the reviewed notices.
The February briefs were drafts for refinement/review, and the September recommendation is not treated as enacted law.
No item-specific reuse permission for data, articles, briefs or maps was verified.
nextAction: Locate or request the NSAP extract and metadata behind the 2015–2024 goby share; obtain landing-center/reach mapping, taxonomic composition, catch units and effort denominators; retrieve the technical bunog assessment and its biomass/reference-point and maturity methods; locate final policy briefs and formal issuances; verify data/map reuse terms. No request has been sent.

sources.supports: Official update reporting gobies as 20.22 percent of total Abra River catch in 2015–2024 NSAP data; no raw extract, taxon breakdown, landing-center/reach crosswalk, method or effort denominator is published.

Official notice of a February 2026 policy-review workshop for the Abra River System goby-fry fishery spanning Regions I and CAR; two policy briefs were still under refinement and review before publication.
Official stakeholder notice identifying bunog as largesnout goby (Awaous melanocephalus) and reporting management figures/recommendations; no assessment, raw series or methods are published.
